subject: Clarification: timezone cutoff / snapshot timestamps for SOC 2 coverage (bridge letter request)
messages:
From: Priya Sen <priya@azura-audit.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lena Park <security@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Clarify SOC 2 timeframe: timezone cutoff & point-in-time snapshots

Hi Hannah,

Quick question as we're preparing the SOC 2 Type II workpapers for Acme Analytics: your SOC 2 report indicates an audit period end date of 2026-12-31. For evidence collection and log exports, can you confirm how Redwood interprets that end date:

- Is the period inclusive through 2026-12-31 23:59:59 in the customer's local timezone, or do you operate on UTC (e.g., 2026-12-31 23:59:59 UTC)?
- When teams pull "point-in-time" snapshots (DB/VM/snapshot IDs), will the exported timestamps be in UTC or in Pacific local time?
- Are monthly coverage statements (e.g., "December 2026 inclusive") understood to include the entire 31st up to 23:59:59 (timezone as above)?

Also: Acme is asking whether a bridge letter will be needed to cover the interim period from 2027-01-01 through 2027-03-31 while we complete testing for the next reporting period. If so, can you confirm who signs and whether Redwood provides a standard bridge template?

Can you provide sample evidence extracts for:
- Audit log export with timezone metadata for 2026-12-31 (showing earliest/latest timestamps)
- Snapshot schedule and actual snapshot timestamps for the final day of the period
- KMS key rotation dates around year-end if there were rotations in Dec 2026

I've attached a short evidence request summary. If easier, we can accept both UTC and local timestamps to avoid ambiguity.

Thanks,
Priya
Senior Auditor
Azura Audit LLP

Attachments: initial_evidence_request.pdf (1 page)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Sen <priya@azura-audit.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, Lena Park <security@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 13:02:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Clarify SOC 2 timeframe: timezone cutoff & point-in-time snapshots

Hi Priya — thanks for the clear list. A few quick answers and next steps from our side: 

- Short answer on interpretation: our standard evidence exports include UTC timestamps by default. For clarity we can produce extracts that include both UTC and Pacific (PST/PDT) offsets where applicable. That should address the inclusive/exclusive ambiguity.

- Point-in-time snapshots: our daily snapshot job runs shortly after midnight UTC (typically ~00:10 UTC). We can pull the 2026-12-31 snapshot and provide the filesystem/VM snapshot IDs along with the UTC timestamp and the local offset.

- Inclusive months: we typically treat a month marked as "inclusive" to cover the full calendar day through 23:59:59 in UTC, unless a customer specifically requests local-time semantics.

- Bridge letter: we do provide a standard bridge letter template for interim coverage; signatory is the Head of Security (I will loop in Marissa to confirm). We can also provide a signed PDF and a DocuSign link.

Next steps: I'll attach the 2026 SOC 2 Type II report for Acme (Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2026.pdf) and a small sample log export for 2026-12-31 showing UTC timestamps. Marissa — can you confirm snapshot run-times and whether we have any KMS rotations in Dec 2026? Connor — can you confirm the correct approver for the bridge letter and whether we should route via DocuSign?

I'll aim to have the log/snaps and bridge template to you by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Compliance
Redwood Inference

I pulled the scheduler and backup logs: our daily snapshot job (global) runs at ~00:10 UTC and creates a snapshot labeled with the UTC timestamp. For 2026-12-31 the snapshot entry is 2026-12-31T00:10:24Z (snapshot-id: snap-20261231-001).

I can also pull a log export with the first and last event for 2026-12-31 showing both UTC and the server-local time (which is set to UTC). If Acme needs local-time (PST) conversions, I can include a second column with the offset.

KMS rotations: our records show no customer KMS key rotation for Acme between 2026-12-01 and 2027-01-15; the last rotation for that key was 2026-11-02.

Bridge letter: we have a standard template and typically the Head of Security signs. For enterprises we can sign and return via DocuSign. I'll upload the snapshot schedule image for your visibility.

Thanks Hannah/Marissa — that's very helpful.

A couple of quick follow-ups before we lock the workpapers: 
- Please include the UTC timestamp in the log export (we've seen systems that only report local time which creates ambiguity).
- For the snapshot evidence, please include the snapshot-id and creation timestamp (UTC). The example you gave (snap-20261231-001 at 2026-12-31T00:10:24Z) looks fine, but we also need an export showing the last event on 2026-12-31 (23:59:59 UTC) to demonstrate coverage to year-end.
- For the bridge letter, please send the standard template via DocuSign and indicate who will sign (Marissa or another Head of Security). Here's the DocuSign placeholder for our records: https://docusign.com/template/abc123.

Once we have the log export with UTC stamps and the signed bridge letter, we can finalize the interim report coverage.
